definition_zh: 狼；色狼；（狼吞虎咽地）吃
definition_en: a wild animal of the dog family that hunts in groups, or to eat food very quickly
core_image: 雪地上排成一线的灰色影子，低着头顺着气味往前赶
scene: 冬夜的雪地尽头，几点灰影成排地跟着气味移动，羊圈里的狗先叫了起来。 A wolf circled the sheep pen twice before the dogs drove it off.
sceneCN: 这里 wolf 是「狼」（第 1 个义项：成群捕食的野生犬科动物）；句意为一只狼绕羊圈走了两圈，才被狗赶走。雪地上排成一线往前赶的灰影，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: keep the wolf from the door

derivatives.zh: 由 wolf 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成，义为「似狼的；贪婪的」
与 wolf 无直接词源关系的动物名，义为「狼獾；貂熊」

senses.title: The wild hunter
senses.definition: a wild animal of the dog family that lives and hunts in groups in forests and open country
senses.definitionCN: 在森林和旷野中成群生活的野生犬科动物
senses.example: A wolf circled the sheep pen twice before the dogs drove it off.
senses.exampleCN: 一只狼绕羊圈走了两圈，才被狗赶走。
senses.why: The word has named this animal since the oldest English records, so the animal is the whole meaning of the root.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从最早的英语文献起就指这种动物，所以动物的形象就是词根的全部意思。

senses.title: The predator of people
senses.definition: a man who hunts women in a cruel and unwanted way, used as a strong word of blame
senses.definitionCN: 以令人不快的方式纠缠女性的男人，用作强烈的贬斥
senses.example: The neighbours warned her about the wolf who hung around the bus stop.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们提醒她当心那个在公交站附近转悠的色狼。
senses.why: Because the animal is seen as a hunter of the helpless, the name slides onto a person who preys on others.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种动物被看作捕食无助者的猎手，这个名字就滑到了欺压他人的人身上。

senses.title: To eat like a hunter
senses.definition: to eat something very fast and in large bites, as a hungry animal would
senses.definitionCN: 像饿兽一样大口快速地吃
senses.example: He wolfed down two bowls of noodles before the train arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 火车到站前，他狼吞虎咽地吃下了两碗面。
senses.why: Turning the animal into a verb borrows its way of eating, so the name becomes an action.
senses.whyCN: 把动物名词变成动词，是借用了它吃东西的样子，于是名字变成了动作。

senses.title: The false alarm
senses.definition: to keep shouting about a danger that is not there, in the fixed phrase cry wolf
senses.definitionCN: 在没有危险时反复喊危险，用于固定说法 cry wolf
senses.example: If you cry wolf too often, nobody will believe you when it is real.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你总是谎报险情，真出事时便没人信你。
senses.why: The fable of the shepherd boy shows that the animal name can stand for empty warnings.
senses.whyCN: 牧童的寓言说明，这个动物名也可以代表空洞的警报。

intro.en: Wolf is an old Germanic animal name, shared with German Wolf and Dutch wolf, and traced back to a reconstructed root meaning the animal itself.
intro.cn: wolf 是古老的日耳曼语动物名，与德语 Wolf、荷兰语 wolf 同源，可上溯到一个重构词根，意思就是这种动物。

items.en: wulf was the ordinary name of the animal in Old English poetry and law.
items.cn: wulf 是古英语诗歌与法律中这种动物的常称。

items.en: The same name appears across the Germanic languages, which shows how old it is.
items.cn: 同一个名字出现在各门日耳曼语里，可见其古老。

items.en: Norse settlers brought forms such as ulfr, which mixed with the English word.
items.cn: 北欧移民带来 ulfr 这样的形式，与英语词混在一起。

items.en: The plural wolves settled in, keeping the old change of f to v between vowels.
items.cn: 复数 wolves 固定下来，保留了元音之间 f 变 v 的古老规则。

items.en: The animal sense stayed, and the verb to wolf down grew out of its greedy eating.
items.cn: 动物义保留至今，动词 wolf down 则由它贪婪的吃相长出来。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same animal stem, the second holds other wild hunters and their kin.
note.cn: 第一组收同根而生的词，第二组收其他野生猎手及其同类。

entries.definition: More than one wolf.
Looking or behaving like a wolf.
Eats something very quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 狼吞虎咽（第三人称单数）

entries.definition: A small wild animal of the dog family with a pointed face.
A wild animal like a small wolf that often feeds on dead animals.
A wild animal of North America, like a small wolf.

normalIntro.en: Wolf is short and old: three consonants frame one round vowel, and only the plural changes its shape.
normalIntro.cn: wolf 又短又古老：三个辅音夹着一个圆元音，只有复数会变形。

normal.en: The w at the front and the lf at the back hold the vowel like jaws.
normal.cn: 前面的 w 和后面的 lf 像上下颌一样夹住元音。

normal.en: Plural wolves keeps the old habit of turning f into v between vowels.
normal.cn: 复数 wolves 保留了元音之间 f 变 v 的老习惯。

normal.en: Wolf down means to eat as fast as a hungry wolf.
normal.cn: wolf down 就是像饿狼一样吃得飞快。

normal.en: Cry wolf comes from the fable of the shepherd boy.
normal.cn: cry wolf 来自牧童的寓言。

normal.en: A lone wolf is a person who keeps away from the group, just like the animal that hunts alone.
normal.cn: lone wolf 指离群的人，正如独自捕猎的狼。

abstract.en: Grey shapes moving in a line through snow.
abstract.cn: 雪地上一排灰影顺着一条线移动。

abstract.en: A ring of eyes at the edge of the firelight.
abstract.cn: 火光边缘围成一圈的眼睛。

abstract.en: Hunger made visible as a body that never stands still.
abstract.cn: 饥饿变成了一个永不停下的身体。

examples.en: A wolf howled somewhere behind the hill and the whole village fell silent.
examples.cn: 山后某处传来一声狼嚎，整个村子静了下来。

examples.en: Do not cry wolf unless you really see the danger.
examples.cn: 除非真的看到危险，否则不要谎报险情。

examples.en: The boy wolfed down his breakfast and ran for the school bus.
examples.cn: 男孩狼吞虎咽地吃完早饭，跑着去赶校车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呜尔夫」——夜里一声长长的「呜」，就是狼在叫。

root: 古英语 wulf（狼），源自日耳曼语共同词形，与德语 Wolf 同源；复数 wolves 保留了 f 在元音间变 v 的古规则。

sensesIntro.en: The animal comes first, then the person who preys on others, then the act of eating like the animal, then the empty alarm.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有动物，再有像动物一样欺压别人的人，接着是像动物一样吃，最后是空洞的警报。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey hunter moving in a line through snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：雪地上一线前行的灰色猎手。

branches.en: The animal branch: a wolf circling the sheep pen.
branches.cn: 动物分支：绕着羊圈转的狼。

branches.en: The human branch: the name turned into an insult.
branches.cn: 人分支：名字变成了骂词。

branches.en: The eating branch: the animal name becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 吃分支：动物名变成动词。

branches.en: The alarm branch: the animal stands for a false warning.
branches.cn: 警报分支：动物代表虚假的警告。

branches.en: The character branch: the way a creature eats becomes a way a person eats.
branches.cn: 品性分支：动物的吃法成了人的吃法。

intro.en: Wolf is a single native stem with no living prefix or suffix; the plural ending is the only inflection it carries.
intro.cn: wolf 是一个单独的本土词干，不带活的词缀；它唯一的屈折变化是复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, so no Latin ancestor exists; the Latin words below are distant cousins from the same old family.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是同属古老语系的远亲。

items.meaning: a wild animal of the dog family
items.example: The stem carries the whole meaning.
It appears in wolfish and werewolf.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 wolfish 与 werewolf 里。

items.example: It forms wolfish, like a wolf.

items.meaning: a man who becomes a wolf
items.example: The old word for man joins the stem.
items.exampleCN: 「人」的古词与这个词干合在一起。

items.meaning: a large dog bred to hunt wolves
items.example: Hound is the old word for dog.
The animal name colours the sound.
items.exampleCN: 动物名为这个声音染上色彩。

definition_zh: 大使；使节；（品牌或事业的）代表
definition_en: the senior diplomat sent by a country to another, or a person who represents a brand or cause
core_image: 大使馆门前，一位身着正装的人递交国书
scene: 新任大使在总统府递交国书，随后与当地官员握手寒暄。 The new ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
sceneCN: 这里 ambassador 是「大使」（第 1 个义项：一国派往另一国的最高外交代表）；句意是新任大使在总统府递交国书。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：大使的；大使级的
名词：女大使；大使夫人，旧用法
名词：大使馆；使馆全体人员
名词：大使职位

senses.title: A country's top diplomat
senses.definition: the senior official who represents one country's government in another country
senses.definitionCN: 一国政府派驻另一国的最高级别代表
senses.example: The new ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 新任大使在总统府递交了国书。
senses.why: The word goes back to a medieval term for a mission or service, so an ambassador is the person sent to carry out that mission abroad.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到中世纪表示「使命、差事」的词，所以大使就是被派往国外执行这项使命的人。

senses.title: A representative of a brand or cause
senses.definition: a well-known person who publicly represents a company, charity, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 公开代表某公司、慈善机构或理念的知名人物
senses.example: The retired player became an ambassador for the children's charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退役球员成了该儿童慈善机构的代言人。
senses.why: A diplomat speaks for a country, and modern marketing borrowed that role: the brand ambassador speaks for a brand in public.
senses.whyCN: 外交官代表国家发声，现代营销借用了这个角色：品牌代言人在公众场合代表品牌。

intro.en: Ambassador came into English from French, and its deeper origin is a word for service or mission.
intro.cn: ambassador 经法语进入英语，更早的来源是表示「服务、使命」的词。

items.en: A Celtic word ambactus meant 'servant, retainer', and it passed into Latin.
items.cn: 凯尔特语 ambactus 意为「仆人、随从」，并传入拉丁语。

items.en: ambactia meant 'service, mission', the duty a retainer carried out.
items.cn: ambactia 意为「服务、使命」，即随从承担的任务。

items.en: French named the person who carried out such a mission, and English borrowed the form.
items.cn: 法语用 ambassadeur 指执行这类使命的人，英语借用了这一形式。

items.en: English ambassador first meant a messenger or representative of a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 ambassador 最初指君主的信使或代表。

items.en: The diplomatic sense became fixed, and the twentieth century added the brand ambassador.
items.cn: 外交义固定下来，二十世纪又增添了品牌代言人的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the embassy family; the near-meaning group ranks diplomatic roles.
note.cn: 形近组是使馆词族；近义组按外交职级排列。

entries.definition: the office and staff of an ambassador
relating to an ambassador
a female ambassador or ambassador's wife
a messenger or representative sent on a special mission
an official who represents a country abroad
an official who protects citizens in a foreign city

normalIntro.en: An ambassador is the person sent on the mission.
normalIntro.cn: ambassador 就是被派去执行使命的人。

normal.en: Embassy is the building, ambassador is the person.
normal.cn: embassy 是使馆建筑，ambassador 是人。

normal.en: Ambassador to a country, not ambassador in.
normal.cn: 说 ambassador to 某国，而不是 ambassador in。

normal.en: Brand ambassador borrows the diplomatic role.
normal.cn: brand ambassador 借用了外交角色。

normal.en: Recall an ambassador when relations break down.
normal.cn: 关系破裂时会把大使召回。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节。

abstract.en: Picture credentials handed over in a palace.
abstract.cn: 想象在总统府递交国书。

abstract.en: See a flag and a formal handshake.
abstract.cn: 想象国旗与正式握手。

abstract.en: Imagine a famous face speaking for a charity.
abstract.cn: 想象名人替慈善机构发声。

examples.en: She was appointed ambassador to Norway last year.
examples.cn: 她去年被任命为驻挪威大使。

examples.en: The ambassador met the foreign minister for talks.
examples.cn: 大使会晤外长进行会谈。

examples.en: The singer acts as an ambassador for a wildlife charity.
examples.cn: 这位歌手担任一家野生动物慈善机构的代言人。

dict_mnemonic.text: ambassador 与 embassy 同族：使馆里那位最高代表，就是大使。

root: 源自凯尔特语 ambactus「仆人、随从」，经中世纪拉丁语 ambactia「服务、使命」与古法语 ambassadeur 于十四世纪进入英语，先指君主的信使，后固定为驻外最高外交代表，现代又引申出品牌代言人。

sensesIntro.en: One role, the mission's representative, now covers both diplomacy and public advocacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 「使命的代表」这一角色，如今同时覆盖外交与公共代言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: credentials handed over at a palace.
core.cn: 核心意象：在总统府递交国书。

branches.en: the ambassador to Norway
branches.cn: 驻挪威大使

branches.en: talks with a foreign minister
branches.cn: 与外国外长会谈

branches.en: an ambassador recalled home
branches.cn: 被召回的大使

branches.en: a charity ambassador
branches.cn: 慈善代言人

branches.en: a brand ambassador on tour
branches.cn: 巡回宣传的品牌代言人

intro.en: A Romance word with a compact family around embassy and ambassador.
intro.cn: 这是罗曼语词，围绕 embassy 与 ambassador 有一小族词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin ambactia is the bridge between the Celtic root and the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ambactia 是凯尔特词根与法语词之间的桥梁。

definition_zh: 飞机（英式英语）；（纸或模型）飞机
definition_en: a powered aircraft with fixed wings, called an airplane in American English, or a small model or paper copy of one
core_image: 草地上停着一架白色小飞机，机翼在阳光下投出细长的影子
scene: 第一次坐飞机的男孩把脸贴在舷窗上，看地面一点点变小。 The aeroplane climbed slowly above the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里的 aeroplane 是「飞机」（第 1 个义项：英式英语对固定翼航空器的称呼）；句意是飞机缓缓爬升到云层之上。

pos.zh: 名词：飞机（英式）；纸飞机；飞机模型

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写变体，义为「飞机」
由希腊语「空气」与「航行」两部分构成，义为「航空学」
由「空气」与「水手」两部分构成，义为「飞艇或气球驾驶员」
由「空气」与「跑道」两部分构成，义为「小型机场」

senses.title: A fixed-wing aircraft
senses.definition: a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings, the ordinary British word for an airplane
senses.definitionCN: 有固定机翼的动力飞行器，英式英语里的常用说法
senses.example: The aeroplane climbed slowly above the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机缓缓爬升到云层之上。
senses.why: The word joins Greek aer, air, to Greek planos, wandering: a craft that wanders through the air instead of staying on a fixed path.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语 aer「空气」与 planos「游荡」合在一起：一种在空中游走、不守固定路线的机器。

senses.title: A model or paper copy
senses.definition: a small toy or folded paper object shaped like an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 做成飞机形状的小玩具或折纸物件
senses.example: He folded an aeroplane from a sheet of newspaper and threw it across the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一张报纸折了架飞机，把它扔过房间。
senses.why: Once the word names the shape rather than the machine, any small imitation of that shape can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指的是那个形状而不是那台机器时，任何模仿该形状的小物件都能用这个名字。

intro.en: A French coinage from two Greek pieces, air and wandering.
intro.cn: 一个法语新造词，由「空气」与「游荡」两个希腊部件拼成。

items.en: aer meant the lower air, the misty layer near the earth, as opposed to the clear upper sky.
items.cn: aer 指靠近地面的雾气层，即下层空气，与高处的清澈天空相对。

items.en: planos meant wandering or roaming, from the verb planasthai, to stray about.
items.cn: planos 意为「游荡的、漫游的」，来自动词 planasthai「四处游走」。

items.en: French coined aéroplane in the mid nineteenth century for an aircraft with fixed wings.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪中期造出 aéroplane，指有固定机翼的飞行器。

items.en: English borrowed the French word and used it first for early experimental flying machines.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语词，最初用来指早期的实验飞行器。

items.en: British English keeps aeroplane, while American English settled on airplane after the Wright brothers' flights.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 aeroplane，美式英语则在莱特兄弟飞行之后定下 airplane。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek element for air; the second collects the everyday words for flying machines.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「空气」的希腊成分；第二组收日常说「飞行器」的几个词。

entries.definition: the American spelling and word for the same machine
entries.definitionCN: 同一机器的美式说法与拼写

entries.definition: the science of flight and aircraft design
a small airport, especially in British usage
a traveller in a balloon or airship
any vehicle that flies, including helicopters; broader than aeroplane
entries.definitionCN: 任何飞行器，包括直升机；范围比 aeroplane 宽

entries.definition: the short everyday word for an aeroplane
an aircraft driven by jet engines
an aircraft that flies without an engine

normalIntro.en: Two Greek pieces, air and wandering, plus the French ending that names a machine.
normalIntro.cn: 两个希腊部件「空气」与「游荡」，加上法语里指机器的词尾。

normal.en: aero- means air, and -plane here comes from a Greek word for wandering.
normal.cn: aero- 表示「空气」，这里的 -plane 来自希腊语「游荡」。

normal.en: British travellers say aeroplane; American travellers say airplane.
normal.cn: 英国旅客说 aeroplane，美国旅客说 airplane。

normal.en: A paper aeroplane keeps the shape but loses the engine.
normal.cn: 纸飞机保留了形状，却没有了发动机。

normal.en: The same aero- appears in aerodrome and aeronautics.
normal.cn: 同一个 aero- 也出现在 aerodrome 与 aeronautics 中。

normal.en: Spell it with aero-, not airo-.
normal.cn: 拼写用 aero-，不要写成 airo-。

abstract.en: Picture a white machine wandering through a grey sky like a fish through water.
abstract.cn: 想象一架白色机器像鱼游过水一样，在灰色天空里游走。

abstract.en: See a child's hand release a folded wing that wanders to the far wall.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子的手放开一只折出的翅膀，它一路游荡到远墙。

abstract.en: Imagine the same word shrinking from a machine to a toy and keeping its name.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词从机器缩成玩具，却仍留着原来的名字。

examples.en: The aeroplane from Paris landed ten minutes late.
examples.cn: 从巴黎飞来的飞机晚了十分钟降落。

examples.en: They crossed the mountains by aeroplane instead of by train.
examples.cn: 他们没有坐火车，而是乘飞机越过群山。

examples.en: A paper aeroplane sailed from the back row to the teacher's desk.
examples.cn: 一架纸飞机从后排滑到讲台上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱若普兰」——爱若飘在空气里，就折成一架飞机让它慢慢游。

root: 法语 aéroplane 由希腊语 aer「空气」与 planos「游荡的」构成，十九世纪中期造出，指固定翼飞行器；英语借入后成为英式常用词。

sensesIntro.en: One sense names the machine, the other names the shape; both go wandering through the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项指那台机器，另一个义项指那个形状；两者都在空中游走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white machine wandering through a grey sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架白色机器在灰色天空中游走。

branches.en: a plane climbing above the clouds
branches.cn: 爬升到云上的飞机

branches.en: a late flight from Paris
branches.cn: 从巴黎晚点到达的航班

branches.en: a folded paper wing crossing a classroom
branches.cn: 飞过教室的折纸翅膀

branches.en: a model hanging from a child's ceiling
branches.cn: 挂在孩子房间天花板上的模型

branches.en: the machine and its small imitation
branches.cn: 机器本身与它的小小仿制品

intro.en: A Greek word for air, a Greek word for wandering, and a French ending.

definition_zh: 空心的；凹陷的；空洞的；挖空

definition_zh: 推测；猜测；投机
definition_en: to guess about something without firm evidence, to think deeply, or to risk money on a possible profit
core_image: 几个人围在桌旁低声讨论一个尚无答案的问题，桌上摊着零散的线索
scene: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。 People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.

senses.title: To guess
senses.definition: to form an opinion without firm evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在没有确凿证据的情况下形成看法
senses.example: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
senses.exampleCN: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。
senses.why: This is the central modern sense of guessing.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示猜测的核心含义。

senses.title: To think deeply
senses.definition: to think about a subject in a deep or abstract way
senses.definitionCN: 以深入或抽象的方式思考某一主题
senses.example: The philosopher speculated about the nature of time.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家沉思时间的本质。
senses.why: The older sense names quiet thought rather than guesswork.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的含义指安静的思考，而非猜测。

senses.title: To risk money

senses.exampleCN: 他炒房产赔了钱。
senses.why: A guess about prices turned into a financial gamble.
senses.whyCN: 对价格的猜测，变成了金融上的赌博。

definition_zh: 授权；使有能力；增强自信
definition_en: to give someone power, authority, or confidence to act
core_image: 把一串钥匙交到新人手里，让他自己做决定
scene: 这项法律赋予公民更多权利。 The law empowers citizens with more rights.
sceneCN: 这里 empower 是「授权」（第 1 个义项：给予某人权力或权利）；句意：这项法律赋予公民更多权利。

senses.title: To give power or authority
senses.definition: to give someone the legal or official power to do something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事的法律或官方权力
senses.example: The law empowers citizens with more rights.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律赋予公民更多权利。
senses.why: The prefix em- puts power into a person, so the word names the transfer of authority.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 em- 把权力放入一个人身上，因此这个词命名权力的转移。

senses.title: To build confidence and ability
senses.definition: to help someone feel able and confident to take action
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人感到有能力、有信心采取行动
senses.example: Good teachers empower their students.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师让学生更有能力。
senses.why: Power can be personal as well as official, so the word also covers growing confidence.
senses.whyCN: 权力既可以是官方的，也可以是个人的，因此这个词也涵盖自信的增长。

senses.title: To enable an action
senses.definition: to make an action or process possible for someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某人能够采取行动或推进过程
senses.example: The new tool empowers small teams.
senses.exampleCN: 新工具让小团队也能做成事。
senses.why: Once people have the means, they can act, so empowerment is also practical enablement.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们有了手段就能行动，因此赋权也是实际上的使能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key placed in an open hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙被放进张开的手掌。

branches.en: The base sense is granting official power.
branches.cn: 基本义是授予官方权力。

branches.en: Power also grows as personal confidence.
branches.cn: 权力也以个人自信的形式增长。

branches.en: Having means makes action possible.
branches.cn: 拥有手段让行动成为可能。

branches.en: Authority and confidence both free a person to act.
branches.cn: 权威与自信都让人得以行动。

branches.en: Confidence turns ability into practice.
branches.cn: 自信把能力变成实践。

intro.en: Empower joins the prefix em-, meaning into, with the noun power.
intro.cn: empower 把意为「进入」的前缀 em- 与名词 power 结合。

latinIntro.en: The prefix em- is a Latin form of in-, while power itself comes from Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 em- 是拉丁前缀 in- 的变体，而 power 本身来自古法语。

items.example: The prefix em- puts power in.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 em- 把力量放入。

items.example: Power is the heart of empower.
items.exampleCN: power 是 empower 的核心。
empowering 标记正在进行的动作。

definition_zh: 按字母顺序地
definition_en: in the order of the alphabet, from A towards Z
core_image: 手指顺着卡片盒里的分隔卡，从 A 抽到 Z
scene: 档案室新来的实习生把所有客户资料按字母顺序排了一遍。 The intern filed the customer records alphabetically.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabetically 是「按字母顺序地」（第 1 个义项：依照字母表先后排列）；句意是实习生把客户资料按字母顺序归档。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：按字母顺序的
名词：字母表
动词：按字母顺序排列
名词：字母编排

senses.title: In A-to-Z order
senses.definition: following the sequence of the alphabet when arranging or naming things
senses.definitionCN: 在排列或列举事物时依照字母表的先后次序
senses.example: The books on the shelf are arranged alphabetically by author.
senses.exampleCN: 书架上的书按作者姓氏的字母顺序排列。
senses.why: The adverb is the -ly form of alphabetical, so it describes how an action such as filing, sorting, or listing is carried out, not what a thing is.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 alphabetical 的 -ly 形式，因此它说明归档、分类、列举等动作是怎样进行的，而不是说明事物本身是什么。

senses.title: By initial letter
senses.definition: using only the first letter as the basis for grouping, as in simple address books
senses.definitionCN: 只以首字母作为分组依据，如简易通讯录的做法
senses.example: For speed, the volunteers grouped the forms alphabetically rather than by date.
senses.exampleCN: 为求速度，志愿者们按首字母给表格分组，而不是按日期。
senses.why: In practice many lists never reach the second letter, so the adverb often means merely grouping under initials, a looser version of full alphabet order.
senses.whyCN: 实际使用中很多清单根本排不到第二个字母，所以这个副词常只表示按首字母分组，是完整字母顺序的宽松版本。

intro.en: Alphabetically is a three-layer word: Greek letter names, a Latin adjective, and an English adverb ending.
intro.cn: alphabetically 有三层构造：希腊字母名、拉丁形容词、英语副词词尾。

items.en: The first two Greek letter names joined to name the whole set.
items.cn: 希腊头两个字母名连起来，用来指整套字母。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century through Latin.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective with -ical appeared in the seventeenth century for lists and indexes.
items.cn: 带 -ical 的形容词在十七世纪出现，用于清单与索引。

items.en: The native adverb ending -ly was added to the adjective to form alphabetically.
items.cn: 英语本族副词词尾 -ly 加在形容词上，构成 alphabetically。

items.en: Modern filing, libraries, and computers made the word an everyday instruction: sort alphabetically.
items.cn: 现代档案、图书馆与计算机使这个词成为日常指令：按字母排序。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family; the near-meaning group offers other sorting adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组属于同一词族；近义组给出其他排序方式副词。

entries.definition: in letter order
the letter set
to put into letter order
in order of time
in order of number
according to a fixed method

normalIntro.en: Alphabetical plus -ly: the adverb of A-to-Z sorting.
normalIntro.cn: alphabetical 加 -ly：A 到 Z 排序的副词。

normal.en: If the action follows the alphabet, use alphabetically.
normal.cn: 动作依照字母表进行，就用 alphabetically。

normal.en: Sort alphabetically is the standard filing instruction.
normal.cn: sort alphabetically 是标准的归档指令。

normal.en: The -ly tells you it describes a verb.
normal.cn: -ly 告诉你它修饰的是动词。

normal.en: It answers the question 'in what order'.
normal.cn: 它回答的是「按什么顺序」。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: al-pha-BET-i-cally.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：al-pha-BET-i-cally。

abstract.en: Picture fingers walking through divider cards.
abstract.cn: 想象手指从一张张分隔卡上划过。

abstract.en: See a spreadsheet sorted by the first column.
abstract.cn: 想象表格按第一列排序。

abstract.en: Imagine a librarian putting A before B.
abstract.cn: 想象图书管理员把 A 放在 B 前。

examples.en: Please arrange the name tags alphabetically before the guests arrive.
examples.cn: 请在客人到之前把名牌按字母顺序摆好。

examples.en: The contact list is sorted alphabetically by surname.
examples.cn: 通讯录按姓氏的字母顺序排序。

examples.en: She filed the invoices alphabetically so the auditors could find them quickly.
examples.cn: 她按字母顺序把发票归档，好让审计人员快速找到。

dict_mnemonic.text: alphabet（字母表）加 -ical（……的）再加 -ly（地）：按字母表地。

root: 由 alphabet 加形容词后缀 -ical 再加副词词尾 -ly 构成。alphabet 源自希腊语头两个字母名 alpha 与 beta，经拉丁语 alphabetum 进入英语；十七世纪出现形容词，副词随后用于描述归档与排列的方式。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb normally means full A-to-Z order, but often shrinks to grouping by initial.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词通常指完整的 A 到 Z 顺序，但常缩为按首字母分组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers flipping through A, B, C divider cards.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指翻过 A、B、C 分隔卡。

branches.en: books shelved by author
branches.cn: 按作者排列的书

branches.en: a contact list sorted by surname
branches.cn: 按姓氏排序的通讯录

branches.en: invoices filed for audit
branches.cn: 为审计归档的发票

branches.en: forms grouped under initials
branches.cn: 按首字母分组的表格

branches.en: a quick address book by first letter
branches.cn: 按首字母编排的简易通讯录

intro.en: An adverb built from a Greek-Latin noun, a Latin adjective ending, and a native English suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由希腊拉丁名词、拉丁形容词词尾与英语本族后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: The -ical ending is Latin in origin, so the relevant Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: -ical 词尾源自拉丁语，因此这里列出相关拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 硬纸板；纸板似的
definition_en: thick stiff paper used for making boxes and simple models
core_image: 压厚的纸，硬得能自己立起来
scene: 他们把书装进硬纸箱里搬走。 They packed the books into cardboard boxes and moved them.
sceneCN: 这里 cardboard 是「硬纸板」（第 1 个义项：做箱子用的厚纸板）；句意是他们把书装进硬纸箱里搬走。

derivatives.zh: cardboard 加 -y 构成，义为「像硬纸板一样的」
构成 cardboard 的第二个成分，义为「板」
构成 cardboard 的第一个成分，义为「卡片、硬纸片」

senses.title: Thick stiff paper for boxes
senses.definition: very thick stiff paper, often with layers pressed together
senses.definitionCN: 非常厚而硬的纸，通常由几层压合而成
senses.example: The package was wrapped in cardboard.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹用硬纸板包着。
senses.why: Card meant a stiff sheet and board meant a plank, so together they name a paper plank.
senses.whyCN: card 指硬纸片，board 指板，合起来就是「纸做的板」。

senses.title: Flat and lifeless, like a cutout
senses.definition: used about a character or story that seems flat and unconvincing
senses.definitionCN: 形容人物或故事扁平、不真实、缺乏生气
senses.example: The hero of the novel feels like a cardboard figure.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的主人公像个纸板人，毫无生气。
senses.why: A cardboard cutout has shape but no life, and that image became a metaphor for flat writing.
senses.whyCN: 纸板剪影有形状却没有生命，这个形象就成了「人物扁平」的比喻。

intro.en: Cardboard is a plain compound of two old words, card and board, joined in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: cardboard 是两个古老词语 card 与 board 的直白复合，在十九世纪合成为一个词。

items.en: bord meant a plank or a flat piece of wood, and later a flat surface.
items.cn: bord 指木板或一块平木头，后来也指平面。

items.en: card named a stiff sheet of paper used for writing or play.
items.cn: card 指用于书写或游戏的硬纸片。

items.en: Box makers began pressing layers of paper into stiff sheets and called the result cardboard.
items.cn: 制盒匠开始把纸层压成硬片，并把成品称为 cardboard。

items.en: Cheap cardboard boxes and toys made the word familiar in ordinary shops.
items.cn: 廉价纸箱和纸板玩具让这个词进入普通商店。

items.en: The adjective sense grew from cutouts, describing characters that are flat and lifeless.
items.cn: 形容词义从纸板剪影引申而来，形容扁平、没有生气的人物。

note.en: Cardboard is a transparent compound, and its neighbours are other thick paper products.
note.cn: cardboard 是词义透明的复合词，邻居是别的厚纸制品。

entries.definition: a small stiff sheet of paper
entries.definitionCN: 小片硬纸，是 cardboard 的第一个成分。

entries.definition: a long flat piece of wood or other hard material
entries.definitionCN: 长而平的木板或其他硬质板材，是第二个成分。

entries.definition: a container made of thick paper
entries.definitionCN: 厚纸做的容器，常由硬纸板制成。

entries.definition: thick paper used for packaging
entries.definitionCN: 包装用的厚纸板，与 cardboard 几乎同义。

entries.definition: stiff board made by pasting layers of paper
entries.definitionCN: 把纸层粘合而成的硬纸板，较旧的说法。

entries.definition: a container with flat sides, often made of cardboard
entries.definitionCN: 有平直侧面的容器，常用硬纸板制成。

normalIntro.en: Two easy pieces: card plus board equals a paper board.
normalIntro.cn: 两个简单部件：card 加 board 就是「纸做的板」。

normal.en: card gives the paper sheet, board gives the flat stiffness.
normal.cn: card 提供纸片，board 提供平板的硬度。

normal.en: cardboard box is the phrase you will meet most often.
normal.cn: cardboard box 是你最常遇到的搭配。

normal.en: The word is uncountable, so one says a sheet of cardboard.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数，所以说 a sheet of cardboard（一张硬纸板）。

normal.en: The adjective sense comes from cutouts: flat shape, no life.
normal.cn: 形容词义来自纸板剪影：只有形状，没有生命。

normal.en: carton is the box made from this material, a useful neighbour.
normal.cn: carton 是用这种材料做的盒子，是有用的邻词。

abstract.en: Picture a flat brown sheet standing upright without bending.
abstract.cn: 想象一张棕色平板自己立着，不会弯下去。

abstract.en: Picture a box folded from one piece of thick paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一个箱子由一整片厚纸折成。

abstract.en: Picture a life-size figure cut from board, smiling but not moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从纸板剪出的真人大小人形，笑着却不动。

examples.en: They packed the books into cardboard boxes and moved them.
examples.cn: 他们把书装进硬纸箱里搬走。

examples.en: The package was wrapped in cardboard.
examples.cn: 包裹用硬纸板包着。

examples.en: The hero of the novel feels like a cardboard figure.
examples.cn: 这部小说的主人公像个纸板人，毫无生气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡板」——卡片压成板，就是硬纸板。

root: 由 card（硬纸片）与 board（板）复合而成，十九世纪定型；card 源自拉丁语 charta（纸）。

sensesIntro.en: A material and a metaphor: stiff paper for boxes, and flatness for lifeless characters.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个材料，一个比喻：做箱子的硬纸，以及形容人物扁平的「纸板感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: layers of paper pressed into a sheet stiff enough to stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸层被压成一张硬得能立起来的板。

branches.en: The material sense: thick paper used for boxes and models.
branches.cn: 材料义：做箱子和模型用的厚纸。

branches.en: The metaphorical sense: a figure with shape but no inner life.
branches.cn: 比喻义：有形状却没有内在生命的形象。

branches.en: cardboard box and cardboard tube name common objects made from it.
branches.cn: 硬纸箱与硬纸筒是这种材料的常见制品。

branches.en: Both senses rest on stiffness: strong enough to hold a shape, but hollow inside.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「硬」上：足够撑出形状，里面却是空的。

branches.en: Critics call a flat character cardboard, borrowing the cutout image.
branches.cn: 评论者把扁平人物称为 cardboard，借用的正是纸板剪影的形象。

intro.en: Cardboard is a compound of card and board, not an affixed form.
intro.cn: cardboard 是 card 与 board 的复合词，不是加词缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Only the first element has a Latin past: card goes back to charta, paper.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第一个成分有拉丁来源：card 可追溯到 charta（纸）。

items.example: The model was built from cardboard.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型是用硬纸板做的。

items.example: Write the address on the card.
The notice was pinned to the board.
Paperboard is sold by the sheet.

items.meaning: board made by pasting paper layers
items.example: The old book had a pasteboard cover.
items.exampleCN: 这本旧书是硬纸板封面。

items.example: He opened a carton of juice.
The box was too heavy to lift.
items.exampleCN: 这个箱子重得抬不起来。

items.example: The bread had a cardboardy texture.

definition_zh: 贼；小偷；偷窃者
definition_en: a person who steals things from another person or place, especially secretly and without violence
core_image: 黑影伸手进别人的口袋：拿走不属于自己的东西
scene: 集市散场时,他的钱包不见了。 A thief slipped the wallet out of his pocket in the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 thief 是「小偷」（第 1 个义项：以隐蔽手段偷窃的人）；句意：人群中小偷把钱包从他口袋里摸走了。

collocations.phrase: set a thief to catch a thief
collocations.zh: 以贼擒贼；以其人之道还治其身

collocations.phrase: like a thief in the night

derivatives.zh: 偷窃；盗窃（行为）（同根名词，指偷窃这一行为而非人）
偷窃（罕见动词形式，由名词逆构）
偷；窃取（ thief 的行为动词，非同根）
扒手（ thief 的具体类型，指在人群中行窃者）

senses.title: A person who steals secretly
senses.definition: a person who takes things that belong to others, secretly and without using force
senses.definitionCN: 暗中取走他人财物、不使用暴力的人
senses.example: A thief broke into the car and took the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷撬开汽车拿走了收音机。
senses.why: The word names the person by the act: to thieve is to take, and the thief is the taker.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以行为命名其人：thieve 是拿走，thief 就是拿走的人。

senses.title: One who takes dishonestly in general
senses.titleCN: 偷窃者；窃取他人成果的人
senses.definition: a person who takes credit, ideas, or time that is not rightfully theirs
senses.definitionCN: 窃取本不属于自己的荣誉、点子或时间的人
senses.example: He called his rival a thief of other people's ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 他称对手为窃取他人点子的贼。
senses.why: Anything that can be owned can be stolen, so the word walks out of the marketplace into business, art and argument.
senses.whyCN: 凡可拥有的皆可被窃，于是这个词走出集市，进入商业、艺术与论战。

senses.title: Time or thief of time idiom
senses.titleCN: 偷走时间等无形之物者
senses.definition: something that takes away time, sleep, or opportunity invisibly
senses.definitionCN: 无声无息夺走时间、睡眠或机会的事物
senses.example: The midnight scroll is a thief of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 深夜刷屏是偷走睡眠的贼。
senses.why: The invisible theft is still theft: what quietly removes something of yours earns the old name.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的偷窃仍是偷窃：悄悄拿走你之物者，配得上这个古老的名称。

intro.en: Thief is a native Germanic word, and its f to v plural change (thief, thieves) is a fossil of an old sound rule that still lives in English grammar.
intro.cn: thief 是日耳曼本土词；其复数 f 变 v（thief→thieves）是一条古老音变规则留在英语语法中的化石。

items.en: The common Germanic root Theub, generally reconstructed, meant to steal; it has no relatives in Latin.
items.cn: 公认的日耳曼词根一般重构为 Theub，意为「偷」；它在拉丁语中没有同源词。

items.en: Old English Theof (or Theof) meant thief, with the plural Theofas already showing the v-sound between vowels.
items.cn: 古英语 Theof 意为「贼」，复数 Theofas 已在元音之间显出 v 音。

items.en: Norse Tjof(or tjof)r, a cousin form, supported the northern usage and spelling.
items.cn: 古诺斯语的同源形式支持了北方的用法与拼写。

items.en: Middle English Theef (or thef) developed the modern plural thieves, fixing the f to v alternation.
items.cn: 中古英语确立现代复数 thieves，固定了 f 与 v 的交替。

items.en: Modern English separated thief (the person) from theft (the act), and the plural thieves became the model taught in schools.
items.cn: 现代英语把 thief（人）与 theft（行为）分开，复数 thieves 成为课堂范本。

note.en: The first group holds the thief-theft family; the second gathers words for takers of different kinds.
note.cn: 第一组是 thief-theft 词族；第二组是各类「拿走者」的词。

entries.definition: the act of stealing; the thief commits a theft
entries.definitionCN: 盗窃行为；thief 所犯下的即是 theft

entries.definition: to steal; a rare verb built back from the noun
entries.definitionCN: 偷窃；由名词逆构的罕见动词

entries.definition: a leader; one letter from thief in spelling, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 首领；拼写与 thief 仅一字母之差，词源无关

entries.definition: one who breaks into buildings to steal, usually at night
entries.definitionCN: 夜盗；破门入室行窃者，多在夜间

entries.definition: one who takes property by force or threat, as in a bank robbery
entries.definitionCN: 抢劫者；以武力或威胁取财，如银行劫匪

entries.definition: a thief who steals from pockets in crowds
entries.definitionCN: 扒手；在人群中从口袋行窃的贼

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the Germanic root, the f-v plural, and the thief-theft pair.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：日耳曼词根、f 变 v 的复数、以及 thief-theft 对。

normal.en: Thief ends in f; the plural steals a v: thief, thieves.
normal.cn: thief 以 f 结尾；复数偷来一个 v：thief, thieves。

normal.en: A thief takes people; theft takes things as its object of talk.
normal.cn: thief 指人；theft 指偷窃行为。

normal.en: Burglar breaks in, robber threatens, thief only slips away.
normal.cn: burglar 破门，robber 动武，thief 只是悄然溜走。

normal.en: Set a thief to catch a thief: only a thief knows the thief's roads.
normal.cn: 以贼擒贼：只有贼才认得贼的路。

normal.en: A thief in the night is quiet, which is the whole point.
normal.cn: 夜贼的要义就是安静无声。

abstract.en: A thief is defined by a hand that is not his own.
abstract.cn: 小偷的定义，是一只不属于他的手。

abstract.en: The quietest theft is the one you notice only by the empty space left behind.
abstract.cn: 最安静的偷窃，是你只凭留下的空位才察觉的那次。

abstract.en: Time is the thief that never gets caught.
abstract.cn: 时间是从不被抓获的贼。

examples.en: The thief was caught on camera.
examples.cn: 小偷被摄像头拍了下来。

examples.en: Thieves stole copper cables from the site.
examples.cn: 窃贼从工地偷走了铜缆。

examples.en: Opportunity knocked once, and worry proved a thief of it.
examples.cn: 机会只敲一次门，而忧虑把它偷走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西夫」——夜里偷东西的人最怕「西夫」（警察吹哨声） → thief 小偷

root: 日耳曼本土词：词根一般重构为 Theub「偷」→ 古英语 Theof「贼」；复数经古英语元音间浊化变为 thieves；名词 theft「盗窃行为」同根。

sensesIntro.en: Thief names the secret taker first, then anyone who takes what is not theirs, and finally the quiet stealers of time and sleep.
sensesIntro.cn: thief 先指暗中窃取者，再泛指拿走不属于自己的东西的人，最后指向时间与睡眠的无声窃贼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching quietly for what belongs to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手悄悄伸向属于别人的东西。

branches.en: The plain wrongdoer of property.
branches.cn: 侵害财产的朴素作恶者。

branches.en: The taker of credit and ideas.
branches.cn: 窃取荣誉与点子的人。

branches.en: The invisible thief of time and sleep.
branches.cn: 时间与睡眠的无形窃贼。

branches.en: Both senses need an owner to wrong; theft is always a triangle.
branches.cn: 两义都需要被侵害的所有者；偷窃永远是三角形。

branches.en: The metaphor keeps the silence of the original image.
branches.cn: 比喻保留了原初意象的寂静。

intro.en: Thief has almost no derivational family; the f-v plural and the act noun theft carry the whole grammar of the word.
intro.cn: thief 几乎没有派生词族；f-v 复数与行为名词 theft 承载了它的全部语法。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the family is purely Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；词族纯出日耳曼，拉丁词条留空。

He thieved his way through the fair.

items.meaning: breaking into a building to steal
items.example: Burglary rose in the holiday season.

definition_zh: （餐馆的）服务员；侍者；男招待
definition_en: a man whose job is to bring food and drink to people at tables in a restaurant
core_image: 一只手托着盘子，从几张桌子之间侧身穿过
scene: 晚饭时分，他一手稳着两只盘子，一手拎着水壶，从挤满人的过道里穿过。 The waiter brought the bill without being asked.
sceneCN: 这里 waiter 是「服务员」（第 1 个义项：餐厅里给人上菜上酒的人）；句意为服务员没等招呼就把账单送来了。托盘侧身穿桌的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: ask the waiter for the bill

derivatives.zh: 等待；侍奉
女服务员
等候；服务
候诊室；候车室

senses.title: A man serving at tables
senses.definition: a man employed in a restaurant to bring food and drink and to look after the tables
senses.definitionCN: 餐厅雇用的男子，负责端送饮食并照看餐桌
senses.example: The waiter brought the bill without being asked.
senses.exampleCN: 服务员没等招呼就把账单送来了。
senses.why: The agent ending -er names the one who waits, and serving at table is the oldest surviving job for this word.
senses.whyCN: 表人的 -er 后缀指「侍候的人」，而递菜上桌是这个词留到今天最古老的一份活计。

senses.title: A person who brings something
senses.definition: in older use, anyone who brings something to another person
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法指任何把东西端送给别人的人
senses.example: The waiter of good news was paid a month in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 带来好消息的那个人被预付了一个月的钱。
senses.why: Before the restaurant sense narrowed, a waiter was simply who brought something, and a few old phrases keep it.
senses.whyCN: 在餐饮义收窄之前，waiter 就是端送东西的人，少数旧语中仍见这一层。

senses.title: In compound titles
senses.definition: in job titles such as head waiter, the person in charge of other waiters
senses.definitionCN: 在 head waiter 等职务名中，指管其他服务员的领班
senses.example: The head waiter seated the guests by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 领班把客人安排在窗边。
senses.why: Compound titles simply add a rank word in front, and head names the one at the front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 复合头衔只是在前头加一个表示等级的词，head 就指站在队列最前的那一个。

senses.title: A serving tray stand
senses.definition: in old British use, a small stand or tray used for serving
senses.definitionCN: 旧英式用法中指上菜用的小架子或托盘
senses.example: The waiter stood beside the sideboard with the teapot.
senses.exampleCN: 托盘架立在餐边柜旁，上面放着茶壶。
senses.why: An object that serves the table was named after the one who serves, and the use has almost died out.
senses.whyCN: 为餐桌服务的器物以服务的人命名，这个用法如今几乎消失。

intro.en: Waiter is the French verb waitier and its English form wait plus -er, the person who waits on others.
intro.cn: waiter 是法语 waitier 的英语形 wait 加 -er，指侍候别人的人。

items.en: The root is Germanic and meant to watch or guard, and that sense stood inside the French verb.
items.cn: 这个词根源出日耳曼语，意为看守或警戒，这层意思藏进了法语动词。

items.en: Old French waitier meant to watch, and then to stay expecting, which English took as wait.
items.cn: 古法语 waitier 意为看守，继而指守候，英语以 wait 承之。

items.en: To wait on someone meant to attend to them at table, so a waiter was the one who did it.
items.cn: wait on 某人意为在桌边照应，于是 waiter 就是做这件事的人。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word narrowed to the restaurant trade.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，这个词收窄到餐饮行业。

items.en: The feminine waitress came later as a separate form; many places now use waiter for both.
items.cn: 阴性形式 waitress 后起而独立，如今不少地方用 waiter 兼指男女。

note.en: The first group gathers the waiting family, the second the staff who work the room.
note.cn: 第一组收 waiting 词族，第二组收在餐厅里干活的人。

entries.definition: To stay until something happens, or to attend on someone.
The older feminine form of the same job.
entries.definitionCN: 女服务员，旧的分性形式

entries.definition: The act of waiting, or serving at table.
The plural, with -s added to the whole word.
A neutral word for the same job, now common in America.
One who clears tables, below the waiter in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 清桌杂工，地位低于服务员

entries.definition: One who serves drinks at a counter.
The person who is served.

normalIntro.en: Wait means to attend on, and -er makes the person, so a waiter is simply the one who waits on the table.
normalIntro.cn: wait 有「侍候」之义，-er 表人，所以 waiter 就是在桌边侍候的人。

normal.en: Wait means attend on; add -er and you have the one who attends.
normal.cn: wait 意为侍候，加 -er 就是侍候的人。

normal.en: The verb is two syllables in speech: wait-er.
normal.cn: 口语里是两个音节：wait-er。

normal.en: Waitress is the older feminine form; server is the neutral one.
normal.cn: waitress 是较旧的分性形式，server 是中性的。

normal.en: To wait on a table is what the job means, not to stand and wait.
normal.cn: wait on a table 指在桌边照应，不是站着干等。

normal.en: The head waiter leads the others.
normal.cn: head waiter 带领其余的人。

abstract.en: See a tray balanced on one hand.
abstract.cn: 想托盘稳稳架在一只手上。

abstract.en: Hear a pen tap a pad as an order is taken.
abstract.cn: 听点单时笔在小本上点点划划。

abstract.en: Picture a coat putting a glass down without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想一杯水被放下而几乎没有声音。

examples.en: The waiter wrote down our order on a small pad.
examples.cn: 服务员在小本上记下我们要点的东西。

examples.en: Ask the waiter for another glass, please.
examples.cn: 请向服务员再要一个杯子。

examples.en: He worked as a waiter in the holidays.
examples.cn: 他假期里当过服务员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂它」——你喂它上菜，它喂你吃饭，托盘一端就是它。

root: 日耳曼语「看守」词根 → 古法语 waitier（守候）→ 英语 wait → wait + -er → waiter。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins at watching and attending, so a waiter is one who attends on people, at tables above all.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「看守、守候」开始，所以 waiter 是照应别人的人，最主要的场合就是餐桌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray carried through a noisy room.
core.cn: 核心意象：托盘穿过喧闹的房间。

branches.en: The table branch: a bill set down unasked.
branches.cn: 餐桌分支：不待开口送上账单。

branches.en: The bringer branch: one who brings good news.
branches.cn: 端送分支：带来好消息的人。

branches.en: The rank branch: a head waiter by the window.
branches.cn: 职级分支：窗边的领班。

branches.en: The object branch: an old stand with a teapot.
branches.cn: 器物分支：放着茶壶的旧托盘架。

branches.en: The service branch: somebody who attends on somebody.
branches.cn: 服务分支：某人在照应某人。

intro.en: The verb wait plus -er makes the person; -ress made the old feminine form.
intro.cn: 动词 wait 加 -er 得到表人名词，-ress 曾造出阴性形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word came through French from a Germanic root, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，由日耳曼语词根经法语传入，因此拉丁条目为空。

definition_zh: 无知；愚昧；不知情
definition_en: lack of knowledge or lack of awareness about something
core_image: 一个人站在陌生的路牌前，看不懂上面的文字
scene: 他对当地风俗一无所知，差点冒犯主人。 His ignorance of local customs almost offended the host.
sceneCN: 这里 ignorance 是「无知」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他对当地风俗一无所知，差点冒犯主人。

derivatives.zh: 无知的
无知地
忽视

senses.title: Lack of knowledge
senses.definition: lack of knowledge or learning
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏知识或学问
senses.example: His ignorance of local customs almost offended the host.
senses.exampleCN: 他对当地风俗一无所知，差点冒犯主人。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of not knowing.
senses.whyCN: 这是一般意义上的不知。

senses.title: Lack of awareness
senses.definition: lack of awareness of a particular fact
senses.definitionCN: 对某一具体事实不知情
senses.example: She acted in ignorance of the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 她在不知新规定的情况下行事。
senses.why: Here the missing knowledge is one fact.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺少的是一件具体事实。

intro.en: Ignorance comes from Latin ignorare, to not know.
intro.cn: ignorance 来自拉丁语 ignorare，意为不知道。

items.en: Ignorare meant not to know.
items.cn: ignorare 意为不知道。

items.en: Ignorantia meant lack of knowledge.
items.cn: ignorantia 意为缺乏知识。

items.en: Ignorance meant lack of knowledge.
items.cn: ignorance 意为缺乏知识。

items.en: Ignorance named the state of not knowing.
items.cn: ignorance 指不知的状态。

items.en: Ignorance also names unawareness of facts.
items.cn: ignorance 也指对事实不知情。

note.en: Ignorance is compared with look-alike words and with words for not knowing.
note.cn: 把 ignorance 与形近词以及表示不知的词作比较。

entries.definition: to pay no attention to
lacking knowledge
without knowledge
lack of awareness
lack of experience
lack of knowledge about something

normalIntro.en: Ignorance names the empty space where knowledge should be.
normalIntro.cn: ignorance 指知识本应在位的空缺。

normal.en: His ignorance of local customs caused offence.
normal.cn: 他对当地风俗的无知造成了冒犯。

normal.en: She acted in ignorance of the new rules.
normal.cn: 她在不知新规定的情况下行事。

normal.en: Ignorance is not the same as stupidity.
normal.cn: 无知并不等于愚蠢。

normal.en: He pretended ignorance of the plan.
normal.cn: 他假装不知道这个计划。

normal.en: Education can reduce ignorance.
normal.cn: 教育能减少无知。

abstract.en: Ignorance is a room we have not entered.
abstract.cn: 无知是我们尚未进入的房间。

abstract.en: What we do not know can still harm us.
abstract.cn: 我们不知道的事仍能伤害我们。

abstract.en: Naming ignorance is the first step out of it.
abstract.cn: 承认无知是走出的第一步。

examples.en: His ignorance of local customs almost offended the host.
examples.cn: 他对当地风俗一无所知，差点冒犯主人。

examples.en: She acted in ignorance of the new rules.
examples.cn: 她在不知新规定的情况下行事。

examples.en: Education can reduce ignorance.
examples.cn: 教育能减少无知。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词根记忆 · ignor（不知道）+ -ance（状态）
dict_mnemonic.text: ignor 来自拉丁语 ignorare（不知道），-ance 表示状态，ignorance 就是「不知道的状态」，即无知、不知情。

root: 来自拉丁语 ignorare（不知道）与 ignorantia（无知），经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Ignorance means lack of knowledge or lack of awareness.
sensesIntro.cn: ignorance 表示缺乏知识或不知情。

core.en: A gap where knowledge has not arrived.
core.cn: 知识尚未抵达的空隙。

branches.en: Ignorance is not the same as stupidity.
branches.cn: 无知并不等于愚蠢。

branches.en: Education can reduce ignorance.
branches.cn: 教育能减少无知。

branches.en: She acted in ignorance of the new rules.
branches.cn: 她在不知新规定的情况下行事。

branches.en: Not knowing a rule is one kind of ignorance.
branches.cn: 不知道一条规则是无知的一种。

branches.en: He pretended ignorance of the plan.
branches.cn: 他假装不知道这个计划。

intro.en: Ignorance belongs with the verb ignore and the adjective ignorant.
intro.cn: ignorance 与动词 ignore、形容词 ignorant 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ignorare, not to know, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ignorare（不知道）是这一词族的来源。

items.example: He was ignorant of the rule.
items.exampleCN: 他对这条规则一无所知。
对风险不知情是危险的。

latinEntries.example: Ignorare is the root of ignore.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ignorare 是 ignore 的词根。

definition_zh: 扶手椅
definition_en: a comfortable chair with supports for your arms
core_image: 一把带两个扶手的宽大椅子，坐下去像被手臂抱住
scene: 他在壁炉边坐下，翻开了那本旧书。 He settled into his armchair by the fire and opened the old book.
sceneCN: 这里 armchair 是「扶手椅」（第 1 个义项：带扶手的单人座椅）；句意是他在壁炉边的扶手椅上坐下，翻开旧书。

pos.zh: 名词：扶手椅；单人沙发椅
形容词：只停留在口头上的，书斋式的（如 armchair critic）

collocations.zh: 只靠阅读图片旅行的「沙发旅行家」

derivatives.zh: armchair 的基础词，义为「椅子」
armchair 的构词成分，义为「手臂」，此处指椅子两侧的扶手
相关上位词，义为「座位；座椅（总称）」

senses.title: A chair with arm supports
senses.definition: a comfortable chair for one person, with parts on each side to rest the arms on
senses.definitionCN: 供单人乘坐的舒适座椅，两侧有可搁手臂的部件
senses.example: Grandfather reads the newspaper in his armchair every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父每天早上都坐在扶手椅里看报纸。
senses.why: The compound is literal: arm plus chair names the chair by its two armrests.
senses.whyCN: 复合词取字面义：arm（手臂）加 chair（椅子），用两侧扶手来命名这种椅子。

senses.title: Involving no real experience
senses.definition: based on reading or imagining rather than real practical experience
senses.definitionCN: 只靠阅读或想象，而非亲身实践得来的
senses.example: He is an armchair critic who has never run a business himself.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个没亲手经营过企业的空谈批评家。
senses.why: The image of the armchair is the seat of comfort and watching, so the word extends to anyone observing life from that seat instead of acting.
senses.whyCN: 扶手椅的画面是安逸旁观之位，由此引申指坐在椅上袖手旁观、不肯亲身实践的人。

intro.en: Armchair is an English compound, built from two native words.
intro.cn: armchair 是英语本土复合词，由两个本族语词拼成。

items.en: arm meant the limb of the body, from Proto-Germanic *armaz.
items.cn: arm 指身体的手臂，来自原始日耳曼语 *armaz（重构形式）。

items.en: chair came via Old French chaire from Latin cathedra, 'a seat'.
items.cn: chair 经古法语 chaire 来自拉丁语 cathedra，义为「座位」。

items.en: The compound armchair is first recorded in the 1600s for chairs with armrests.
items.cn: 复合词 armchair 首见于十七世纪，指带扶手的椅子。

items.en: The figurative sense grew in the 1800s: the armchair became the symbol of staying comfortably at home.
items.cn: 十九世纪出现比喻义：扶手椅成了足不出户、安逸旁观的象征。

items.en: The literal furniture sense is still the main one; the figurative use survives in set phrases.
items.cn: 字面的家具义仍是主义；比喻义保留在若干固定搭配中。

note.en: Words nearby in form are other compound chairs; words nearby in meaning describe comfort or sitting.
note.cn: 形近词多为其他复合家具词；近义词与舒适、就座相关。

entries.definition: the part of a chair where you rest your arm
entries.definitionCN: 椅子上供搁手臂的部分，即扶手；与 armchair 同含 arm 一词

entries.definition: a chair on wheels used by people who cannot walk
entries.definitionCN: 带轮子的椅子，供不能行走的人使用；同为 chair 复合词，结构平行

entries.definition: a large fleet of warships
entries.definitionCN: 舰队；只是开头拼写 arm 相近，词源与 armchair 无关，来自西班牙语

entries.definition: a long comfortable seat for two or more people
entries.definitionCN: 供两人以上的长沙发；比 armchair 大，坐的人多

entries.definition: a long comfortable seat, the everyday word for sofa
entries.definitionCN: 长沙发的日常说法，与 sofa 基本同义

entries.definition: an armchair whose back can be tilted backwards
entries.definitionCN: 椅背可后仰的躺椅；可视为 armchair 的一种

normalIntro.en: Break the compound into its two native parts and picture the arms.
normalIntro.cn: 把复合词拆成两个本族语部分，想象出那两只「手臂」。

normal.en: arm + chair = a chair with arms.
normal.cn: arm（手臂）+ chair（椅子）＝带「手臂」的椅子，即扶手椅。

normal.en: The two armrests are the chair's arms hugging you.
normal.cn: 两条扶手就是椅子伸出来搂住你的两只手臂。

normal.en: Compare wheelchair: same pattern, chair named by its feature.
normal.cn: 对比 wheelchair（轮椅）：同一构词法，用特征命名椅子。

normal.en: An armchair traveller never leaves the chair, only reads.
normal.cn: armchair traveller（沙发旅行家）人不离椅，只靠阅读环游世界。

normal.en: Arm in arm, arm to armrest, arm to chair.
normal.cn: 由「手臂」顺藤摸瓜：手臂→扶手→带扶手的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture sinking into a big chair that embraces you with two arms.
abstract.cn: 想象陷进一把大椅子，它伸出两只手臂把你抱住。

abstract.en: The armchair is the throne of doing nothing.
abstract.cn: 扶手椅是「什么都不干」的王座，安逸旁观者的宝座。

abstract.en: From the armchair you can see the whole world on TV without moving.
abstract.cn: 坐在扶手椅里不用动，就能从电视里看遍全世界——空谈与远眺之位。

examples.en: She fell asleep in the armchair in front of the fire.
examples.cn: 她在壁炉前的扶手椅里睡着了。

examples.en: There is an old leather armchair in the corner of the study.
examples.cn: 书房角落里有一把旧皮扶手椅。

examples.en: Don't be an armchair critic; come and help us instead.
examples.cn: 别做空谈的批评家了，过来帮我们吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿姆切尔」——阿姆（arm，手臂）搭在椅儿（chair）上，扶手椅就是有两只手臂的椅子。

root: 英语本土复合词：arm（手臂，源自原始日耳曼语 *armaz，重构形式）+ chair（椅子，经古法语 chaire 来自拉丁语 cathedra「座位」）。字面即「带手臂的椅子」，指两侧有扶手。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal piece of furniture, the word extends to people who experience life only from that seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面的家具义出发，引申指只坐在那把椅子上、不经实践便妄加评论或想象的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair with two arms that hold the sitter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把伸出两只手臂搂住坐者的椅子。

branches.en: The literal chair with armrests.
branches.cn: 字面义：带扶手的座椅。

branches.en: The armrests give comfort, the seat invites you to sink in and stay.
branches.cn: 扶手带来舒适，座椅诱人陷进去不动。

branches.en: Staying seated means watching instead of doing.
branches.cn: 坐着不动，即旁观而非行动。

branches.en: From watching come opinions formed without experience.
branches.cn: 由旁观生出未经实践的意见。

branches.en: Both senses hinge on the picture of arms: the chair's and the metaphorical embrace of comfort.
branches.cn: 两个义项都系于「手臂」的画面：椅子的扶手，以及安逸的隐喻怀抱。

intro.en: Armchair is a native compound; the useful pieces are arm and chair and the pattern of naming a thing by its feature.
intro.cn: armchair 是本土复合词，可拆解的构件是 arm 与 chair，以及「以特征命名事物」的构词模式。

latinIntro.en: Only chair has a Latin ancestor; arm is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 chair 有拉丁祖先；arm 是日耳曼本族词。

items.meaning: arm of the body; hence armrest
a seat, naming the chair by its kind or feature
items.meaningCN: 椅子，作复合词后一部分，以种类或特征命名

items.meaning: a band worn around the arm
items.meaningCN: 戴在手臂上的带子，如袖章
items.example: The referee wore a red armband.

items.meaning: the part of the arm between elbow and wrist
items.meaningCN: 肘与腕之间的部分，前臂
items.example: He rolled up his sleeves to the forearm.

items.meaningCN: 军队；与 arm（手臂）词源无关，来自拉丁语 arma「武器」
items.example: He joined the army last year.

items.meaning: a chief church, from Latin cathedra 'seat' (of a bishop)
items.meaningCN: 大教堂；与 chair 同出拉丁语 cathedra「主教之座」
items.exampleCN: 我们参观了那座古老的大教堂。

items.meaning: with official authority, literally 'from the chair'
items.meaningCN: 以权威身份发言，字面义「自宝座上」
items.example: The professor spoke ex cathedra on the subject.
items.exampleCN: 教授以权威口吻谈论该问题。

items.meaning: the person presiding over a meeting
items.meaningCN: 主席；原指「坐椅子（主持）的人」

latinEntries.meaningCN: 座位；主教的宝座，是 chair 的最终来源

latinEntries.meaning: down + seat, a seat with a back
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一般认为由希腊语 kata（向下）+ hedra（座位）构成，指带靠背的座位

latinEntries.meaning: a seat, a place of sitting
latinEntries.meaningCN: 座位；拉丁语中与 hedra 同义的常用词

definition_zh: 急性的；敏锐的；严重的；锐角的
definition_en: sharp, severe, or sudden in onset
core_image: 一根针尖闪出寒光，尖端细得几乎看不见
scene: 医生判断这是急性阑尾炎，要求立刻安排手术。 The doctor called it acute appendicitis and ordered surgery at once.
sceneCN: 这里的 acute 是「急性的」（第 1 个义项：发病急、病程短的疾病类型）；句中指急需处理的阑尾炎。

pos.zh: 急性的；敏锐的；严重的；锐角的

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「强烈地；敏锐地」
加名词后缀 -ness，义为「敏锐；剧烈」
同源名词，义为「（感官的）敏锐度」
同源名词，义为「精明、洞察力」

senses.title: A disease that comes sharply
senses.definition: describing an illness that begins suddenly and is short but severe
senses.definitionCN: 形容发病突然、病程较短但症状较重的疾病
senses.example: The doctor called it acute appendicitis.
senses.exampleCN: 医生称之为急性阑尾炎。
senses.why: Latin acutus meant sharpened, and physicians used it for a disease whose onset cuts in sharply rather than creeping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acutus 意为「磨尖的」，医生用它形容来势像刀割一样突然、而不是慢慢拖的病。

senses.title: A very sharp sense or mind
senses.definition: able to notice or understand things quickly and clearly
senses.definitionCN: 能够迅速而清楚地察觉或理解事物的
senses.example: Dogs have an acute sense of smell.
senses.exampleCN: 狗的嗅觉非常敏锐。
senses.why: A sharpened edge cuts easily, so the same image was applied to hearing, sight and judgement that cut to the point.
senses.whyCN: 磨尖的刃容易切开东西，于是同一意象被用到听觉、视觉与判断力上：一下就切中要害。

senses.title: Severe and urgent
senses.definition: very serious and needing quick attention
senses.definitionCN: 非常严重、需要立即处理的
senses.example: The city faces an acute shortage of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临严重缺水。
senses.why: If a condition is sharp, it hurts now, so acute shifted from sudden illness to any problem at its most intense.
senses.whyCN: 状况「尖锐」就意味着当下就疼，于是 acute 从突然发病扩展到任何处于最紧张程度的问题。

senses.title: An angle below ninety degrees
senses.definition: describing an angle smaller than a right angle
senses.definitionCN: 形容小于直角的角
senses.example: The two lines meet at an acute angle.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条线以一个锐角相交。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the oldest sense: an acute angle is the sharpest kind of corner, the one that looks like a point.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了最古老的含义：锐角是最尖的一类角，看上去就像一个针尖。

intro.en: The word starts from the Latin name for a needle and the verb to sharpen.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语里「针」的名称和「磨尖」的动词出发。

items.en: acus meant a needle.
items.cn: acus 意为针。

items.en: acuere meant to sharpen or to whet.
items.cn: acuere 意为磨尖、磨快。

items.en: acutus described anything sharpened, including pain and fever.
items.cn: acutus 形容一切被磨尖的东西，包括疼痛与发热。

items.en: acute entered medicine for sharp fevers and later for sharp senses.
items.cn: acute 先进入医学，指来势凶的发热，后来才指敏锐的感官。

items.en: geometry added the acute angle, the sharpest corner of all.
items.cn: 几何学又添上「锐角」，即最尖的那种角。

note.en: The first group shares the sharp root; the second names other ways of being intense.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「尖」的词根；第二组是别的表示「强烈」的词。

entries.definition: intensely, sharply
sharpness
sharpness of sense
attractive, originally sharp
having a fine edge
very bad or intense
quick to notice
at a turning point

normalIntro.en: Sharp is the single picture behind the illness, the mind and the angle.
normalIntro.cn: 「尖」是贯穿疾病、心思与角度的同一个画面。

normal.en: Acute and chronic are a pair: sharp and short against long and slow.
normal.cn: acute 与 chronic 是一对：急而短，对慢而长。

normal.en: An acute angle is under ninety degrees, the sharp one.
normal.cn: 锐角小于九十度，是最尖的那个角。

normal.en: The noun acuity keeps the same sharp idea.
normal.cn: 名词 acuity 保留了同样的「尖锐」。

normal.en: The comparative uses more, because the word is long.
normal.cn: 这个词较长，比较级用 more。

normal.en: Do not confuse acute with a cute, which is far softer.
normal.cn: 别把 acute 与 cute 混同，后者语气柔软得多。

abstract.en: See a needle point catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针尖在光下闪出亮线。

abstract.en: Picture a sudden pain that makes a person stop walking.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵突如其来的痛让人停住脚步。

abstract.en: Think of two lines closing to a narrow point.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线收拢成一个很窄的尖角。

examples.en: He felt acute pain in his chest.
examples.cn: 他感到胸口一阵剧痛。

examples.en: Her acute hearing caught the whisper across the room.
examples.cn: 她敏锐的听觉捕捉到了房间另一头的低语。

examples.en: The region faces an acute shortage of doctors.
examples.cn: 这个地区严重缺乏医生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿Q特」——阿Q特别敏感，一点风吹草动就觉得疼，医生说是急性发作。

root: 拉丁语 acutus（磨尖的），源自 acuere（磨快）与 acus（针）；由「尖」这一核心意象分出四个方向：发病急、感官敏锐、问题严重、角小于直角。

sensesIntro.en: One sharp image branches into illness, perception, severity and geometry.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「尖」的意象，分叉到疾病、感知、严重程度与几何。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle point shining in the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：光下闪亮的针尖。

branches.en: an illness that cuts in suddenly
branches.cn: 突然切进来的疾病

branches.en: senses that catch the smallest detail
branches.cn: 能捕捉最细小动静的感官

branches.en: a problem at its most intense
branches.cn: 处于最紧张程度的问题

branches.en: a corner narrowed to a point
branches.cn: 收窄成一个点的角

branches.en: sharpness shared by illness and crisis
branches.cn: 疾病与危机共有的「尖锐」

intro.en: A needle root plus a Latin participle ending gives the sense of sharpened.
intro.cn: 表示「针」的词根加上拉丁分词词尾，得到「被磨尖的」。

latinIntro.en: The same root gives acumen, acuity and acupuncture.
latinIntro.cn: 同一词根还给出 acumen、acuity 与 acupuncture。

definition_zh: 精细地；细小地；很好地
definition_en: into very small pieces, with great delicacy, or in a very good way
core_image: 刀刃落下，洋葱被切成几乎透明的薄片
scene: 厨师把洋葱切得很细。 The chef chopped the onions finely.
sceneCN: 这里 finely 是「细小地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：厨师把洋葱切得很细。

derivatives.zh: 精细的
精细
提炼

senses.title: With delicate skill
senses.definition: with delicate care or detailed workmanship
senses.definitionCN: 以细致的用心或工艺完成的
senses.example: The wood was finely carved.
senses.exampleCN: 这块木头雕刻得很精细。
senses.why: This sense stresses careful craft.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项强调用心的手艺。

senses.title: Into tiny pieces
senses.definition: cut or ground into very small pieces
senses.definitionCN: 被切碎或磨成很小的颗粒
senses.example: The chef chopped the onions finely.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师把洋葱切得很细。
senses.why: Thin pieces are called fine.
senses.whyCN: 细碎的小块被称为 fine。

senses.title: Very well
senses.definition: in a very good or excellent way
senses.definitionCN: 以很好、很出色的方式
senses.example: She performed finely under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下表现得很好。
senses.why: Fine quality extends to how an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 优良的品质也延伸到做事的程度上。

intro.en: Finely is fine plus the adverb suffix -ly, so it inherits the whole history of fine.
intro.cn: finely 由 fine 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，因此继承了 fine 的全部历史。

items.en: Finis meant an end or limit.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Fin meant finished or perfected.
items.cn: fin 意为完成的或完善的。

items.en: Fine meant of high quality.
items.cn: fine 意为品质优良的。

items.en: The adverb finely described delicate action.
items.cn: 副词 finely 描述细致的动作。

items.en: Finely also came to mean in tiny pieces.
items.cn: finely 又引申为「细碎地」。

note.en: Finely is compared with similar-looking words and with adverbs of precision.
note.cn: 把 finely 与形近词以及表示精确的副词作比较。

entries.definition: of good quality
last in order
in a strong way
in a gentle and careful way
in an exact way
in a thin layer

normalIntro.en: Finely tells how something is done with care or cut into tiny pieces.
normalIntro.cn: finely 说明动作是精细完成的，或被切成细小的部分。

normal.en: Chop the herbs finely.
normal.cn: 把香草切碎。

normal.en: The fabric is finely woven.
normal.cn: 这块布料织得很精细。

normal.en: A finely tuned engine runs smoothly.
normal.cn: 调校精良的引擎运转顺畅。

normal.en: The balance is finely set.
normal.cn: 这个平衡调得很微妙。

normal.en: Finely ground coffee smells strong.
normal.cn: 磨得很细的咖啡香气浓烈。

abstract.en: Precision is patience made visible.
abstract.cn: 精确是耐心变得可见的样子。

abstract.en: Small cuts can shape a larger whole.
abstract.cn: 细小的刀工也能塑造更大的整体。

abstract.en: To do a thing finely is to respect the material.
abstract.cn: 把事情做精细，就是尊重材料本身。

examples.en: The chef chopped the onions finely.
examples.cn: 厨师把洋葱切得很细。

examples.en: The wood was finely carved.
examples.cn: 这块木头雕刻得很精细。

examples.en: The instrument was finely tuned.
examples.cn: 这件乐器被调校得很精细。

dict_mnemonic.text: finely 由 fine（精细的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示「精细地、细碎地」。

root: 由 fine（源自拉丁语 finis，完成、完善）加 -ly 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Finely means with delicate skill, in tiny pieces, or very well.
sensesIntro.cn: finely 意为精细地、细碎地或很好地。

core.en: Doing something in a fine, careful manner.
core.cn: 以精细、用心的方式做某事。

branches.en: Craft done with delicate care.
branches.cn: 以细致用心完成的工艺。

branches.en: Material cut into tiny pieces.
branches.cn: 被切成细碎小块的物料。

branches.en: An action done very well.
branches.cn: 完成得很好的动作。

branches.en: Skill and quality meet in the adverb.
branches.cn: 技艺与品质在这个副词中相遇。

branches.en: Fine pieces and fine performance share one form.
branches.cn: 细碎与出色共用一个形式。

intro.en: Finely is formed by adding the adverb suffix -ly to the adjective fine.
intro.cn: finely 由形容词 fine 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The base fine goes back to Latin finis, an end.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 fine 上溯至拉丁语 finis（结束）。

items.example: Fine threads are hard to see.

The fineness of the sand surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 沙子的细度让我们惊讶。

items.example: They refine metal in this plant.
items.exampleCN: 他们在这家工厂提炼金属。
这个设计还需要进一步改进。

latinEntries.example: Finis lies behind fine and finely.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finis 是 fine 与 finely 的词源根基。

definition_zh: 不安的；心神不宁的；不自在的；令人不安的；不稳定的
definition_en: slightly worried or uncomfortable, or making people feel that something is wrong
core_image: 坐在椅子上却怎么也找不到一个安稳的姿势
scene: 深夜的病房里，家人守着还没出结果的化验单，谁也坐不住。 The silence in the waiting room made everyone uneasy.
sceneCN: 这里 uneasy 是「心神不宁的」（第 1 个义项：心里不踏实）；句意为候诊室里的沉默让每个人都坐立不安。找不到安稳姿势的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不安地；局促地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不安；局促」
去掉否定前缀 un- 后的肯定形式，义为「容易的；从容的」

senses.title: Feeling worried without a clear reason
senses.definition: slightly worried or nervous, often without being able to say why
senses.definitionCN: 有点担心或紧张，往往说不出具体缘由
senses.example: She felt uneasy about the phone call and could not sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那通电话感到不安，翻来覆去睡不着。
senses.why: The prefix means not, and the base word means at ease, so uneasy is literally not at ease.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「安逸、自在」，因此 uneasy 字面上就是「不自在」，不安从这里直接生出。

senses.title: Awkward in company
senses.definition: not comfortable in a social situation, as if you do not know what to do with yourself
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中不舒服，手脚都不知往哪里放
senses.example: He gave an uneasy laugh and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他局促地笑了一下，换了个话题。
senses.why: The same lack of ease that keeps the body restless also shows in a voice or a laugh.
senses.whyCN: 让身体坐立难安的那份不自在，同样会从嗓音和笑声里露出来。

senses.title: A silence or mood that suggests trouble
senses.definition: used of a silence, mood, or peace that seems to hide a problem
senses.definitionCN: 形容沉默、气氛或和平似乎掩盖着问题
senses.example: An uneasy silence fell over the table after his remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他那一句话之后，桌上一片令人不安的沉默。
senses.why: A feeling of not being at ease spreads from people to the room they sit in.
senses.whyCN: 不自在的感觉会从人传到人所在的屋子，于是空气本身也显得不安。

senses.title: A relationship or arrangement that may not last
senses.definition: used of a peace, alliance, or agreement that is forced and may break down
senses.definitionCN: 形容被迫达成、随时可能破裂的和平、联盟或协议
senses.example: The two sides reached an uneasy truce before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在入冬前达成了勉强的停战。
senses.why: Anything that leaves people not at ease is also likely to fall apart.
senses.whyCN: 任何让人无法安心的安排，往往也难以长久维持。

senses.title: Sleep that is broken and shallow
senses.definition: used of sleep that is light and full of waking moments
senses.definitionCN: 形容睡得浅、常常醒来的睡眠
senses.example: After a night of uneasy sleep she went back to the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 睡了一夜不踏实的觉，她又回到了医院。
senses.why: The body that cannot settle by day cannot settle at night either.
senses.whyCN: 白天找不到安稳姿势的身体，夜里同样安稳不下来。

intro.en: The word is a plain English construction: un- plus easy, with the mental sense of easy coming from Old French.
intro.cn: 这个词是地道的英语构造：un- 加 easy，而 easy 的「安逸」之义来自古法语。

items.en: The prefix un- was already used to reverse the meaning of a word.
items.cn: 古英语时期，前缀 un- 已用于反转词义。

items.en: Aise meant comfort or leisure, and the phrase at ease entered English from it.
items.cn: aise 意为「舒适、闲暇」，短语 at ease 由此进入英语。

items.en: Ease and easy grew from that source and meant free from pain or trouble.
items.cn: ease 与 easy 由这一来源发展而来，意为「无痛无扰」。

items.en: Uneasy is formed by adding the negative prefix to easy and appears in writing in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: uneasy 由否定前缀加 easy 构成，十六世纪见于书面记录。

items.en: The sense widens to silences, alliances, and sleep, wherever a calm surface hides strain.
items.cn: 此后意义扩展到沉默、联盟与睡眠，只要平静的表面下藏着紧张就能用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other un- adjectives about attitude, while the near-meaning group collects words for fear.
note.cn: 形近组收集其他表示态度的 un- 形容词，近义组汇集表示担忧害怕的词。

entries.definition: not difficult, or free from worry
in a worried or awkward way
not firm or stable
entries.definitionCN: 不稳的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: not common
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常的（只是前缀相同，词根不同）

entries.definition: worried about what may happen
unable to stay still
slightly frightened or tense
peaceful and not worried

normalIntro.en: Nothing in the word is exotic: a negative prefix rests on a word for comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词一点也不生僻：一个否定前缀压在一个表示舒适的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus easy: not at ease is exactly what uneasy means.
normal.cn: un- 加 easy：不在自在的状态，就是 uneasy 的本义。

normal.en: Feel uneasy about something is the most common frame for learners.
normal.cn: feel uneasy about 是学习者最常用的搭配框架。

normal.en: Uneasiness is the state, uneasily the manner of moving or speaking.
normal.cn: uneasiness 是那种状态，uneasily 是那种说话或动作的样子。

normal.en: An uneasy silence and an uneasy alliance both point to tension under the surface.
normal.cn: an uneasy silence 与 an uneasy alliance 都指向表面之下的紧张。

normal.en: Compare at ease, which means relaxed, to see the negative in action.
normal.cn: 对比 at ease（放松、自在）就能看清否定前缀的作用。

abstract.en: Picture hands on a chair arm, fingers tapping and stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手搭在椅臂上，手指敲了又停。

abstract.en: Hear a joke, then a laugh one beat too late.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话，然后是一声慢了半拍的笑。

abstract.en: Feel a room where everyone has decided not to say the obvious thing.
abstract.cn: 体会一个所有人都绕着明摆着的话说的房间。

examples.en: He was uneasy about leaving his mother alone in the house.
examples.cn: 他不放心把母亲一个人留在家里。

examples.en: An uneasy calm settled on the village after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，村子笼罩在一片令人不安的平静里。

examples.en: She smiled uneasily at the doctor and closed the door behind her.
examples.cn: 她对医生不安地笑笑，然后关上了身后的门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺意贼」——钱包里少了钱，俺心里就惦记着那个贼，坐也坐不稳。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ easy（安逸的），easy 义源自旧法语 aise（舒适、闲暇），短语 at ease 即由此而来

sensesIntro.en: A single state, not being at ease, spreads from the body to voices, rooms, agreements, and sleep.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份状态，不自在，从身体蔓延到嗓音、房间、协议与睡眠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that cannot find a settled position.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副怎么也摆不稳的身体。

branches.en: The private branch: a vague worry with no clear cause.
branches.cn: 私密分支：说不出缘由的隐约担忧。

branches.en: The social branch: the body that does not know how to stand.
branches.cn: 社交分支：身体不知该怎么摆。

branches.en: The atmosphere branch: a room that hints at a hidden problem.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：屋子暗示着藏起来的问题。

branches.en: The arrangement branch: a peace everyone expects to break.
branches.cn: 安排分支：人人都知道待不住的和平。

branches.en: The nightly branch: sleep that keeps coming apart.
branches.cn: 夜间分支：总是断开的睡眠。

intro.en: The word is built from a negative prefix and a borrowed adjective, so its parts are easy to read.
intro.cn: 这个词由否定前缀与借入的形容词搭成，部件一眼可辨。

latinIntro.en: The base word is not Latin, but the Old French aise behind it may come from Latin adjacens, lying near.
latinIntro.cn: 词根本身不是拉丁语，但其后的旧法语 aise 可能源自拉丁语 adjacens（邻近的）。

items.example: Uneasy means not easy in comfort.
He glanced uneasily at the door.

items.exampleCN: 一种奇怪的不安充满了她。

definition_zh: 宇航员；航天员；航天飞行乘组成员
definition_en: a person who is trained to travel and work in a spacecraft
core_image: 一个穿着白色宇航服的人被绑进座椅，身后是火箭尾焰和漆黑天空
scene: 电视直播里主持人激动地说： The astronaut floated into the space station and waved at the camera.
sceneCN: 这里指「乘航天器进入太空的人」（第 1 个义项：接受训练乘航天器上太空的人）；句意为宇航员飘进空间站，对着镜头挥手。

pos.zh: 宇航员；航天员；乘航天器进入太空的人

derivatives.zh: 航天学；航天技术
天文学家（共享 astro- 词根，但研究而非飞行）
天文学
（俄方）宇航员
（中方）航天员

senses.title: A trained space traveler
senses.titleCN: 受训乘航天器进入太空的人
senses.definition: a person trained by a space program to travel and work aboard a spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 由航天计划训练、乘航天器进入太空并在其上工作的人
senses.example: The astronaut spent six months aboard the space station.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宇航员在空间站上待了六个月。
senses.why: The word literally means 'star sailor': someone who sails among the stars, so the core image is a person riding a craft through space.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面意思是「星际水手」：在群星间航行的人，所以核心意象是乘飞行器穿越太空的人。

senses.title: A crew member of a space mission
senses.definition: one of the people assigned to fly a particular space mission, whether pilot, scientist or engineer
senses.definitionCN: 被指派执行某次航天飞行任务的人员，无论担任飞行员、科学家还是工程师
senses.example: Each astronaut on the mission had a different job during launch.
senses.exampleCN: 任务中每位宇航员在发射时承担不同的职责。
senses.why: Spacecraft carry crews like ships carry sailors, so astronaut extends to every member of that crew.
senses.whyCN: 航天器像船载水手一样载着乘组，所以 astronaut 扩展到乘组的每一位成员。

senses.title: A national space program title
senses.definition: the English term for space travelers of the US and international programs, contrasted with cosmonaut and taikonaut
senses.definitionCN: 美国及国际计划中航天员的英语称谓，与俄语 cosmonaut、中文 taikonaut 相对
senses.example: An American astronaut and a Russian cosmonaut shared the same capsule.
senses.exampleCN: 一位美国宇航员和一位俄罗斯宇航员共用同一个返回舱。
senses.why: Different space agencies coined their own words from the same Greek roots, so astronaut names one tradition among several.
senses.whyCN: 各国航天机构用同一批希腊词根造了自己的词，astronaut 只是其中一种传统的称呼。

senses.title: A job or career in spaceflight
senses.definition: the profession of flying in space, requiring years of training in engineering, science and survival
senses.definitionCN: 上太空执行飞行任务的职业，需要在工程、科学和生存训练上投入多年
senses.example: She dreamed of becoming an astronaut since primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小学起就梦想成为宇航员。
senses.why: Because training is long and selective, astronaut also names the career itself, like pilot or sailor.
senses.whyCN: 由于训练漫长且选拔严格，astronaut 也像 pilot、sailor 一样指这份职业本身。

senses.title: Figurative use for a space-like experience
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：仿佛置身太空的人
senses.definition: informally, someone in a situation that feels weightless, isolated or otherworldly
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指处于失重、隔绝或仿佛在另一个世界的人
senses.example: With all the noise cancelling on, I felt like an astronaut in my own bubble.
senses.exampleCN: 开着降噪耳机，我感觉自己像置身太空泡泡里的宇航员。
senses.why: The image of a lone figure floating in a white suit is so vivid that people borrow it for any isolated, floating experience.
senses.whyCN: 白色宇航服里孤独漂浮的形象太鲜明，人们借它形容任何隔绝、漂浮般的处境。

senses.title: Historic and pioneer astronauts
senses.definition: people remembered as the first or most famous space travelers, such as Yuri Gagarin or Neil Armstrong
senses.definitionCN: 作为最早或最著名航天者被记住的人，如加加林、阿姆斯特朗
senses.example: Schoolchildren learn the name of the first astronaut who orbited the Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们都要学习第一位绕地球飞行的宇航员的名字。
senses.why: Because spaceflight is young, each milestone astronaut is a named hero in history books.
senses.whyCN: 航天历史很短，每个里程碑式的宇航员都成了史册上有名有姓的英雄。

senses.title: Astronaut in training or candidates
senses.definition: applicants and trainees who have been selected for a space program but have not yet flown
senses.definitionCN: 已被航天计划选中但尚未上天的候选人和受训者
senses.example: The new class of astronaut candidates begins underwater training next month.
senses.exampleCN: 新一届宇航员候选人下月开始水下训练。
senses.why: Selection is so famous that even people who have never left Earth are already called astronauts in the media.
senses.whyCN: 选拔过程太出名，媒体把还没离开地球的受训者就已经称作宇航员。

senses.title: Everyday and childhood usage
senses.definition: used loosely by children or in play for anyone in a space costume or dreaming of space
senses.definitionCN: 孩子游戏或口语中，泛指穿太空服、向往太空的任何人
senses.example: The toddler in a puffy snowsuit waddled across the room like a little astronaut.
senses.exampleCN: 穿着蓬松雪地服的幼儿像小宇航员一样摇摇摆摆地穿过房间。
senses.why: The costume defines the image, so anything bulky and white invites the nickname astronaut.
senses.whyCN: 服装本身定义了形象，任何白色臃肿的装束都会让人联想到宇航员。

intro.en: astronaut is a modern coinage from Greek astro- (star) and naut- (sailor), literally 'star sailor', modeled on words like aeronaut.
intro.cn: astronaut 是现代造词，来自希腊语 astro-（星）和 naut-（水手），字面义为「星际水手」，仿照 aeronaut 一类词构成。

items.en: Greek astron means 'star' and nautes means 'sailor'; neither formed a classical compound astronaut.
items.cn: 希腊语 astron 意为「星」，nautes 意为「水手」；古希腊语中并没有 astronaut 这样的复合词。

items.en: In the 1920s to 1930s, writers coined astronaut on the model of aeronaut, a balloon traveler of the 18th and 19th centuries.
items.cn: 二十世纪二三十年代，作家们仿照十八九世纪的热气球旅行者 aeronaut，造出了 astronaut 一词。

items.en: Early English uses referred to fictional or imagined space travelers before any real spaceflight existed.
items.cn: 在真实航天出现之前，英语里的 astronaut 最早指小说和想象中的太空旅行者。

items.en: After Gagarin's flight in 1961 and the US Mercury program, astronaut became the official title for American space travelers.
items.cn: 1961 年加加林升空及美国水星计划之后，astronaut 成为美国航天员的正式称谓。

items.en: The Soviet program used cosmonaut (kosmos + nautes) and China later used taikonaut, all built on the same sailor image.
items.cn: 苏联计划用 cosmonaut（宇宙 + 水手），中国后来用 taikonaut（太空 + 水手），都基于同一「航行」意象。

items.en: Today astronaut is the general English word for any professional space traveler, whatever their nationality.
items.cn: 今天 astronaut 是英语中对职业航天员的通称，不问国籍。

note.en: Group one collects astro- words that look or build alike; group two collects near-meaning space traveler terms.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或同用 astro- 词根的词；第二组是语义相近的太空旅行者称谓。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies the stars; shares astro- but studies from Earth rather than flying.
entries.definitionCN: 研究星辰的科学家；共享 astro- 词根，但在地面研究而非上天飞行。

entries.definition: The science of celestial objects; the field an astronaut may fly for but is not itself a person.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体的学科；宇航员可能为之飞行，但它本身不是人。

entries.definition: One who reads horoscopes; looks close to astronomer but is not a science profession.
entries.definitionCN: 看星盘占卜的人；与 astronomer 拼写相近，但并非科学职业。

entries.definition: The Russian and Soviet term for a space traveler, built on kosmos instead of astron.
entries.definitionCN: 俄苏航天员的称谓，用 kosmos 而非 astron 构词。

entries.definition: The English word for Chinese space travelers, from taikong (space) plus naut.
entries.definitionCN: 中国航天员的英文称谓，来自「太空」加 naut。

entries.definition: Flies aircraft within the atmosphere; an astronaut pilots spacecraft beyond it.
entries.definitionCN: 在大气层内驾驶飞机；宇航员在大气层外驾驶航天器。

normalIntro.en: Remember astronaut as a sailor of the stars: astro- star + naut sailor.
normalIntro.cn: 把 astronaut 记成「星际水手」：astro- 星 + naut 水手。

normal.en: astro- means star, as in astronomy; naut means sailor, as in nautical.
normal.cn: astro- 表示星（如 astronomy）；naut 表示水手（如 nautical 航海的）。

normal.en: cosmonaut and taikonaut share the same -naut tail; only the first part changes by country.
normal.cn: cosmonaut、taikonaut 共用 -naut 尾，只有前半随国家不同。

normal.en: An astronaut trains for years before riding a rocket.
normal.cn: 宇航员上天前要训练好几年。

normal.en: aeronaut (balloon sailor) was the model for astronaut.
normal.cn: aeronaut（气球水手）是 astronaut 的构词蓝本。

normal.en: Think of a white spacesuit floating outside the space station.
normal.cn: 想象空间站外漂浮的一袭白色宇航服。

abstract.en: A tiny white figure drifting above a blue marble that holds everyone you know.
abstract.cn: 小小的白色身影，漂浮在容纳你所有熟人的蓝色圆球之上。

abstract.en: The silence of a helmet: your own breath is the loudest sound.
abstract.cn: 头盔里的寂静：自己的呼吸是最响的声音。

abstract.en: A rope between you and the ship — the only thread home.
abstract.cn: 你和飞船之间的一根系绳——回家唯一的线。

examples.en: The astronaut answered questions from students while floating in zero gravity.
examples.cn: 宇航员在失重漂浮中回答了学生们的问题。

examples.en: Only the healthiest candidates are chosen to become astronauts.
examples.cn: 只有最健康的候选人才能被选为宇航员。

examples.en: Astronauts must exercise daily to keep their muscles strong in orbit.
examples.cn: 宇航员在轨道上必须每天锻炼以保持肌肉力量。

dict_mnemonic.text: astro-（星）+ naut（水手）= 星际水手 = 宇航员

root: 希腊语 astron（星）+ nautes（水手）→ 现代仿 aeronaut 造词 astronaut。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one image, a person sailing among the stars: the trained traveler, the mission crew, national titles, the career, figurative use, historic pioneers, trainees and playful usage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由「星际航行的人」这一意象展开：受训的旅行者、任务乘组、各国称谓、职业、比喻用法、历史先驱、受训者、童趣用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-suited sailor floating in black space, tethered to a small ship.
core.cn: 核心意象：白色宇航服的水手漂浮在漆黑太空里，系着一艘小飞船。

branches.en: SPACEFLIGHT: the trained person and their role on a mission crew.
branches.cn: 航天：受训上太空的人及其在任务乘组中的角色。

branches.en: NAMING AND CAREER: national titles like cosmonaut, and spaceflight as a profession.
branches.cn: 称谓与职业：cosmonaut 等各国称谓，以及航天飞行这门职业。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE AND PLAYFUL: anyone who feels space-like or dresses the part.
branches.cn: 比喻与童趣：任何感觉像在太空或穿上太空装的人。

branches.en: HISTORY: the pioneer astronauts remembered by name.
branches.cn: 历史：被记住名字的先驱宇航员。

branches.en: TRAINING: candidates selected but not yet flown.
branches.cn: 训练：已入选但尚未上天的候选人。

intro.en: astronaut is built on Greek astro- (star) and -naut (sailor); the -naut tail also appears in aeronaut, cosmonaut and aquanaut.
intro.cn: astronaut 由希腊语 astro-（星）和 -naut（水手）构成；-naut 尾还出现在 aeronaut、cosmonaut、aquanaut 中。

latinIntro.en: astro- comes from Greek astron; -naut from Greek nautes. Latin passed both shapes into modern scientific coinages.
latinIntro.cn: astro- 来自希腊 astron；-naut 来自希腊 nautes。这两个词形经由现代科学造词沿用至今。
